_about: DRAFT profile for Moksy AI (brand) and Moksy Limited (company), written only from what the repo's own Moksy sources say (content/products/moksy.json and content/brand/moksy-*.json, which cite the brand guidelines, the Moksy Lexicon, docs/SEO.md and the published site pages). Anything those sources do not say is left out, not guessed. Review every answer before publishing. Load with: npm run import:profile -- content/profiles/moksy.json (--dry to preview).

identity.mission: Most software fails in the specification, not the implementation. Moksy works on that problem: it turns an idea into a build-ready plan. AI structures the idea, and vetted experts refine it.
identity.vision: The founder's stated goal is 1:99: 99 percent of the work done by machine and 1 percent by a human. The share is measured, not guessed: every decision is stamped decidedBy as machine or human.
identity.positioning: Every page that ranks for questions such as how much it costs to build an app belongs to an agency that wants to win the build. Moksy is the only voice in the result list not selling the build, and that neutrality is the whole advantage. Moksy never recommends a builder, not even a sister company. The Free plan is a real plan: the same engine reporting on fewer areas, enough to judge whether the thinking is any good. Moksy claims no rights over a customer's plan or the idea behind it, on any plan.
identity.voice: Friendly, professional and confident, in plain language that never adds guesswork. British English everywhere a person reads (organise, colour, analyse, judgement). Moksy is written with a capital M, never MOKSY or moksy. Tagline: "Turn your idea into a build-ready plan." Description: "Idea in, build-ready plan out. AI structures it, vetted experts refine it." Use the lexicon words: Briefing (not interview), Blueprint (not report, plan, spec or document), Areas (not pillars), Peer, Expert and Priority Review. MOX is Moksy credit (1 MOX = $0.01) and MXP is Moksy Experience Points: always pair the unit with its noun (Wallet, Ladder). Headings, buttons and navigation use Title Case; body copy uses sentence case. Never use Ninja, Guru, Mystic, Sage or Master as titles. The retired taglines are "Empowering your digital transformation", "Building Future-Ready Brands" and "AI requirements + expert review".
identity.visual_identity: One accent, a dark ink and neutrals. Primary Moksy orange-red #EF4123, secondary deep petrol #002835, accent grey #6D6E71, text ink #0F172A, canvas #FAFBFC. Orange is the only non-neutral colour used for actions, one primary action per view. Status colours (emerald, amber, rose, indigo) are for state only. Headings in Bebas Neue (font file still to be added), body in Myriad Variable, code in JetBrains Mono. Logo files are local; never link a remote moksy.ai URL as a fallback. Imagery is minimal and icon-led, product and data visuals over stock photography.

goals.review_cadence: Guide results are reviewed at 4, 8 and 12 weeks along the chain impressions, clicks, Blueprints, Pro. Nothing is expected for four to eight weeks, because judging earlier measures the crawler's schedule, not the content.
goals.non_goals: Outbound sales: at the published prices, £100k a year is roughly 280 to 440 paying subscribers, which outbound cannot reach, so growth is treated as a content and search problem. Paid social is not part of the documented motion; any Facebook or Instagram test is new and must earn its place against the same numbers. Recommending a builder, even a sister company.

organisation.decision_rights: A disputed review is adjudicated by a senior reviewer, and that decision settles whether the review counts as accepted. A super admin can pin a user to a level, which freezes automatic computation. Open product choices, such as whether to open any path to withdrawable MOX, are recorded as pending founder decisions.
organisation.escalation: Customers: support@moksy.ai for account, plan, billing, review and broken-feature problems; privacy@moksy.ai for privacy and data requests; legal@moksy.ai for questions about the terms. Buying questions (pricing, procurement, security questionnaires) go to Sales. Disputed reviews go to support and are arbitrated by a senior reviewer.
organisation.hiring: Every job at Moksy starts with a reviewer account. People apply as reviewers, review real plans, and Moksy hires from those doing it well. It hires into fourteen disciplines at junior, mid-weight and senior levels: Solution architect, Technical lead, Backend engineer, Frontend engineer, Data engineer, DevOps engineer, Site reliability engineer, Security engineer, QA engineer, UX designer, UI designer, Product manager, Delivery manager and Business analyst. Moksy says it will not ask for unpaid work as a test, grant accreditation because it likes someone, hire someone a level above where they are so it can pay below it, or keep a vacancy open it does not intend to fill.

offerings.catalogue: Moksy turns an idea into a build-ready plan in five steps, in order: Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build. The customer types in an Idea; Moksy asks questions in a Briefing; the answers become a Blueprint covering up to 22 Areas; reviews check it (Peer Review is free from the community, Expert Review is by an accredited reviewer and included in Pro and Max, Priority Review is paid and returns an Expert Review within 36 hours); Build covers exports, hiring and tools. A Spec Sprint is a one-day, human-led engagement. MOX is Moksy credit, bought in Packs and used for work outside a plan's benefits. One idea and its Blueprint live inside a Project.
offerings.pricing: Plans per month in GBP, excluding VAT unless stated. Free £0: 3 projects, a Starter Blueprint of 5 of 22 areas, standard models, 1 seat, 5 exports a month, no Expert Reviews, no API. Pro £19: 25 projects, a Fuller Blueprint of 12 of 22 areas, advanced models, unlimited Expert Reviews, 5 seats, 100 exports a month, API access. Max £79: unlimited projects, seats and exports, a Complete Blueprint of all 22 areas, the most capable models, unlimited Expert Reviews, API access; Max is the plan that makes someone eligible to become a paid reviewer. Enterprise and public sector are priced separately and include SSO and SCIM, role-based access, a signed DPA, invoicing against a PO, UK data residency and a private reviewer pool. MOX is credit bought once, does not renew, is pegged at 1 MOX = $0.01, and every debit is itemised in the Wallet ledger. Refunds on unused credit are a discretionary review through support, not automatic.
offerings.delivery: Briefing: Moksy asks the questions and gathers the Brief. Blueprint: AI drafts it from the Brief; every recommendation shows its reasoning, and an AI-drafted Blueprint is a draft that can be wrong. Review: a reviewer claims the job from their Queue (scope, window and fee are shown before claiming), reviews section by section, and states what is wrong and why; the customer accepts the corrections or pushes back; fees are released from Escrow once the review is accepted or the response window closes without a dispute. Build: exports, hiring and tools.
offerings.roadmap: Directions recorded in the sources, not committed dates. Move the live customer path onto the pattern dispatcher (the 2026-09-14 brief measured 0 percent coverage; 110 patterns declared, 18 implemented). Replace the twenty fantasy rung titles with the six plain rungs of the lexicon (Candidate to Fellow); the published Levels page currently shows five. Wave 2 of the cost guides: SaaS MVP, marketplace, school website, mobile app versus web app. A Facebook Page import is absent and would need Meta App Review.
offerings.platforms: A Docker-first microservice platform: 25 backend services, two frontends and three shared packages. The gateway is the only public API entry; the dashboard (Vite) and a Docusaurus documentation site are the other public surfaces. Each service owns its own logical database. Stack named in the sources: MongoDB Atlas, Redis, Stripe for payments, OpenAI as a sub-processor, and a local Ollama model as the default for local development.

customers.segments: Six starting points for a project: a booking system, an e-commerce website, a SaaS MVP, a marketplace, a school website and a mobile app. Audience pages on the public site: Founders, Teams and startups, Agencies, Enterprise, Education and Public sector. People words: Guest (not signed in), Member (signed in, on Free), Customer (anyone with a Project), Reviewer (accredited) and Staff (operator).
customers.journey: Idea, Briefing, Blueprint, Review, Build. Before that, the guides are the landing pages: they serve the gap between I have an idea and I have signed an agency, and every guide ends in the same place: a range is not your number, and the free Blueprint is how you get yours. The one primary call to action everywhere is "Start free" ("Get my Blueprint" on the home form only).

customers.support_model: Most answers are in the help centre. Otherwise: support@moksy.ai. Customers should include the account email and, for a plan or review, the link to it. Routes: account or sign-in, plan, billing or credit (with date and amount), reviews and disputes, and anything broken go to support; privacy and data requests to privacy@moksy.ai; legal questions to legal@moksy.ai; buying questions to Sales. Disputed reviews are arbitrated by a senior reviewer. Support should quote the published pages and say so when pages disagree.

ways_of_working.process: Everything runs in Docker; do not run npm install on the host. Local start: copy .env.example to .env, fill the seven mandatory secrets, then npm run dev, npm run seed and npm run seed:personas. Deployment is manual: pushing to GitHub deploys nothing. On the server, git pull and run npm run deploy:prod, which rebuilds only changed services, health-checks, and records the commit (a plan-only preview exists).
ways_of_working.documentation: The README (levels, roles, running locally), the Moksy Lexicon (the shared vocabulary), the brand guidelines, docs/SEO.md (growth motion), the architecture and pattern briefs, the real-jobs learning brief, and the Docusaurus developer documentation site. The published pages (pricing, trust, help, contact support, legal terms and privacy, reviewer pages, careers) are the company's public statements.

risk_register.risk: The platform is about 60 percent of the way to a proper microservice architecture: one shared secret between services, plain http, no message broker, and a gateway controller holding business logic of nearly ten thousand lines.
Guest AI quotas reset when a new session is minted, so inference spend is uncapped and a public free tier gets farmed (launch promo proposal, 13 August 2026).

Published pages disagree with each other (data deletion period, who handles security questionnaires, the sector described in the legal wording, review prices), so support may quote a figure as settled when it is not.
risk_register.what_we_do_about_it: Support quotes pages as published and dated, and confirms before promising.

risk_register.risk: Not ISO 27001 certified and not yet Cyber Essentials certified, which procurement and security questionnaires may ask about.
risk_register.what_we_do_about_it: The trust page says so plainly and will say when that changes.

communications.social: Paid social is not part of the documented growth motion. Ads may only describe what exists and can be evidenced, and any figure must come from a source. No ad should promise a Facebook Page import, which does not exist. Do not quote review values in ads: the promise is the free Blueprint. Ad creative follows the brand voice rules (capital M, Blueprint and Briefing, British English, one primary action).

expansion.markets: Enterprise and public sector offers (priced separately, with SSO, UK data residency and a private reviewer pool). Cost guides in two waves, the second adding SaaS MVP, marketplace, school website and mobile app versus web app.

legal.entity: The terms of service and privacy policy name the contracting party and data controller as Moksy AI Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales. English law and courts apply. Customers must be at least 18.
legal.regulations: UK GDPR, including Article 33 (controllers are notified within 72 hours of Moksy becoming aware of a personal-data breach). Customers may ask for access, correction, deletion, to object or restrict, and portability, and may complain to the ICO. Only strictly necessary cookies are used without consent; optional analytics cookies need explicit consent. Moksy is not ISO 27001 certified and not yet Cyber Essentials certified.
legal.data_handling: Primary data is held in the UK; sub-processors are pinned to UK or EEA regions wherever the service supports it. TLS 1.2 or better in transit, AES-256 at rest for the primary database and its backups. Role-based access with a per-endpoint audit log, quarterly access reviews, and mandatory two-factor authentication for administrators. Personal data is not sold. Audit and ledger rows are anonymised rather than deleted. Sub-processors named: OpenAI, Stripe, MongoDB Atlas and Redis; adding one takes 30 days' notice. Card numbers are not stored (Stripe processes payments). The published deletion period differs between pages (30 days on the trust page, 90 days on the privacy policy, financial records 7 years) and is to be confirmed.
legal.ip_licences: The customer keeps ownership of the data and content they submit and gives Moksy a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to process it solely to provide the services. Moksy claims no rights over a customer's plan or the idea behind it. AI output is provided for information only and is not guaranteed; the customer must review and validate it before relying on it. Moksy's total liability for a claim is capped at what the customer paid in the previous 12 months.

finance.invoicing: Prices are in GBP and exclude VAT unless stated. Premium plans are billed in advance, monthly or annually; payments are processed by Stripe and authorise recurring charges until the customer cancels, which can be done at any time in account settings. Enterprise is invoiced against a purchase order. Reviewer earnings are paid in MOX and withdrawn to money at a published rate (125 MOX to £1 at the time of the source), after a hold of 14, 7 or 3 days depending on the reviewer's membership.
